title: Fortune 500 IT capex bundles AI-PC refresh into data-center spend by H2 2027
body: Nvidia and Microsoft opened a managed-fleet capex category Monday June 1 at GTC Taipei. The RTX Spark Superchip (20 Arm cores co-designed with MediaTek paired with a Blackwell GPU carrying 6,144 CUDA cores and 128GB unified LPDDR5X on a single TSMC 3nm package, hitting 1 petaflop of FP4 AI compute and running 120B-parameter LLMs at 1M-token context locally) ships fall 2026 inside Microsoft's Surface Laptop Ultra as the lead device, with ASUS, Dell, HP, Lenovo, and MSI follow-on systems shipping in the same window — five named PC OEMs in lockstep, the same supply chain already shipping Vera Rubin NVL72 racks fall 2026 across 350+ partners in 30 countries. The structural force is procurement-side. Once a frontier-grade local-inference budget (1 PFLOP FP4, 128GB unified memory, 120B-param LLMs offline) lands inside the OEM channel running corporate-fleet refresh on a 36-month cycle, the CFO question stops being 'do we buy Copilot seats?' and becomes 'do we refresh 40,000 endpoints into AI-PCs against which budget line, before the next Vera Rubin training contract closes?' The Build June 2-3 follow-on closes the architectural loop: the Windows Agent Framework MIT release lets a single YAML manifest run identically on the worker's laptop, the Windows 365 Cloud PC GPU node provisioned overnight, and the on-prem rack the data-center capex paid for. By H2 2027 we expect at least three Fortune 500 IT organizations (likely from the early-Copilot-Studio cohort: JPMorgan, Walmart, Accenture, Pfizer, Honeywell, KPMG) to disclose at investor-day or 10-K MD&A a unified AI-infrastructure capex line bundling managed AI-PC fleet refresh with data-center training and inference spend — replacing the separate end-user-computing and data-center capex lines 10-Ks currently maintain — and at least one Big Four advisory practice (Deloitte, EY, PwC, or KPMG) to publish a public RFP template under that unified-capex framing. The bear case is Surface Laptop Ultra fall-2026 unit-economics slipping past the corporate RFP cycle, signaled by a Q4 2026 Microsoft 10-Q footnote restating Surface volume guidance downward; absent that slip, H2 2027 lands AI-PC managed-fleet refresh as a named line in Fortune 500 AI capex disclosure.

reasoning.because: RTX Spark 1-PFLOP/128GB AI-PC ships fall 2026 across MS Surface + 5 named OEMs in lockstep
reasoning.given: Same OEM channel runs Vera Rubin + 36-mo fleet refresh; Build YAML unifies laptop+Cloud PC+edge
reasoning.so_that: Fortune 500 disclose unified AI-infra capex bundling AI-PC fleet refresh with data-center spend
reasoning.landing: By H2 2027; >=3 Fortune 500 disclosures + 1 Big Four RFP template
reasoning.plain_language: New AI laptops run huge AI models offline, so big companies will start budgeting laptops and AI data centers together.

summary: Nvidia and Microsoft opened an AI-PC managed-fleet category Monday: the 1-PFLOP RTX Spark Superchip (128GB memory, 120B-param local LLMs) ships fall 2026 in Surface Laptop Ultra plus 5 OEM follow-ons. By H2 2027 >=3 Fortune 500 disclose unified capex bundling AI-PC refresh with data-center spend.
